messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@acmeai.com>, Insight Labs <ops@insightlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly pipeline -> fleet synthesis: scenario ask and deliverables

Team — looping you in for this week's fleet planning ask tied to the Acme pilot and broader Q4 pipeline. High level: Acme is targeting a pilot + committed volume that could convert into reserved capacity next year. Sales needs a set of concrete fleet-sizing scenarios so we can correlate commit shapes to reserve slot requests and finance can model ARR/burn.

Key deliverables I need by EOD Fri (2027-08-06):
- A scenario matrix (conservative / base / upside) mapping deal-close timelines to required dedicated-equivalent GPU slots (8xA100 eq) and peak concurrent sessions.
- A short list of infra constraints or lead-time risks (how quickly we can provision extra pools or reassign reserved slots).
- Finance-facing burn/ARR sketch (monthly cost to Redwood, recommended billing cadence for Acme pilot).

Notes and assumptions (please flag changes):
- Target window: Aug -> Dec 2027 (pilot in Sept -> possible ramp Oct-Nov).
- Baseline customer inference footprint provided by Amy: ~120k tokens/day across 3 services, spiky peak around demo times.
- We should include burst credits and autoscale windows in the matrix (how many burst GPUs needed for 48h spikes).

Attachments: scenario-matrix.xlsx (starter), acme-pilot-commit.pdf (customer LOI). I started a lightweight Drive folder (link below) with the model usage export Amy shared.

Why this matters: we want to avoid late-stage surprises where sales asks for reserved slots with 2-week lead time but infra needs 6+ weeks. If we can present a joint plan this Friday, we can set expectations with Acme and lock a staging window for the pilot.

Questions for each owner:
- Karthik: can you validate pool lead times and list what pre-warm options we have?
- Laura: what billing cadence will reduce revenue recognition friction and still look attractive to Acme?
- Ben: given other active pilots, where does Acme sit on priority for burst credits / emergency slots?

Thanks — I'll consolidate and send a summary to Amy and Ops on Monday.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — quick infra reality check and a couple mitigation ideas.

Short answers up front:
- Provisioning lead time for dedicated pools (new physical / reserved zoning) = ~5–7 weeks (procurement + allocation + smoke testing).
- Burst slots (using spare hosted capacity) are available within 24–48 hours but are not SLA-backed.
- Pre-warm options: snapshot images + model cache preload can reduce warm-up to ~2 hours for known model variants.

Details / implications:
- If the win is in Oct and requires >50 8xA100-eq reserved slots, we should start procurement conversations immediately. For smaller asks (<20 slots) consider mixing reserved + scheduled burst windows.
- Quantization and batching knobs can reduce effective slot needs by ~25% for embedding-heavy workloads — we should call this out in the matrix as a note.
- Operational risk: cross-customer preemption rules currently allow us to reassign unfilled reserved capacity; doing so repeatedly increases incident risk and will require an SLA carve-out.

Actionable asks from infra side:
1) Provide scenario slots as "provisioning model" (i.e., how many reserved vs burst vs pre-warm) — I can validate feasibility against current procurement timelines.
2) If sales wants fast turn-up for demos, we can reserve a short 'staging buffer' of 10 slots in Sept with pre-warm images; technical lead time = ~72 hours once pool is assigned.

I'll attach the provisioning runbook excerpt in the Drive folder (internal link).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Folks — finance view and a couple of constraints to call out.

Key points:
- Billing cadence: for a pilot that may convert to reserved next year, monthly invoicing with a 30-day net works best for sales velocity. We can offer a 3-month billed-in-advance option for a small discount if the customer will accept upfront commitment.
- Cost modeling: for the matrix, please include a column for "monthly infrastructure cost to Redwood" and a separate column for "list price to customer". I recommend we model both (conservative: list price - 20% = margin buffer; base: list price - 10%).
- Revenue recognition: if we take prepayment for reserved slots we need clear SOW language; otherwise revenue will be recognized over time. That affects cash flow assumptions in the short term.

Quick numbers (rough, please refine):
- Conservative scenario: 15 8xA100-eq slots -> ~ $74k/mo infra cost -> suggest list price ~$120k/mo.
- Base scenario: 35 slots -> ~ $170k/mo infra cost -> suggest list price ~$275k/mo.
- Upside scenario: 70 slots -> ~ $330k/mo infra cost -> suggest list price ~$520k/mo.

Please treat the above as placeholders — I need the slot breakdown by reserved vs burst so I can produce a clean ARR/burn table. If you can get me that by EOD Fri I will produce a finance-ready PDF (billing-scenarios.pdf) and a short slide for Monday's customer sync.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Finance | Redwood Inference
